title: Design: LoRA-tuned small model vs prompting for ICD-10-CM extraction
scenario: Kestrel measured a prompted large model and a LoRA-tuned 2B open model on the same synthetic held-out notes for ICD-10-CM code suggestions. Decide what ships first with real cost arithmetic and slice-level quality, then design serving inside the HIPAA boundary, release gates and the October 1 code-set update.
task: Compute cost per 1,000 notes, per month and the break-even volume
Analyse quality by slice and recommend what ships first
Design serving, evaluation gates, code-set updates and PHI handling
acceptance: Arithmetic correct and the decision follows from it
Rare codes and invalid codes treated as the costly errors
Deployable architecture and gates inside the HIPAA boundary
